historical_evidence_messages.speaker: client
historical_evidence_messages.text:
Thank you for providing the $1400.00 estimate. That works for me.

A few items:

1) My subcontractors won’t send me their content until EOD next Wednesday, so your working period will be compressed. Would you be able to turn it around within 48-hour of receiving the final narrative content from me, followed by a 24-hour turnaround on your end for the final revisions?

2) For the branding, I’ve shifted the focus from the client’s brand to the bidder’s brand—mine! I’d like the design to reflect my company, Agua Arc. I can provide my logo and colors.

3) Because this will be the first proposal I’m submitting as a prime, and I launched my company less than a year ago and work solo, I’d like to use this proposal as a template going forward. Ideally, the template you build would have modular/swappable sections so future proposals don’t need to be recreated from the beginning. In particular, I’m imagining a) a flexible narrative-section framework, since some proposals may have 5 sections v 8 sections, b) a modular table design that can be resized for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for \_\_\_ \[client name\]” credit line instead of client branding.

4) Regarding Canva, can I own the files without having a paid subscription? Would there be any other source files, or would everything exist solely in Canva?

Thank you!

historical_evidence_messages.speaker: freelancer
historical_evidence_messages.text:
1) That timing is workable for me. To verify the dates, I would spend Thursday the 24th and Friday the 25th preparing the first draft, with revisions taking place on Tuesday the 28th.

2) I’m glad to center the design on Agua Arc's identity rather than GreenLatinos. Please send your logo, colors, and any other materials you’d like me to use as references.

3) The modular template system you’ve outlined would be very valuable to your business over time, but it goes beyond the scope of the quoted work. Designing and testing a system that can adapt to future proposals with different section counts and budget formats requires more work than a one-time layout pass. I’d be happy to develop it, but I’d want to price that work separately so the arrangement remains fair to both of us. Would you like me to quote the modular template as an add-on now, or should we keep this initial proposal straightforward and return to the template as a separate future project?

4) I’ll only use free Canva assets, so the file won’t contain elements restricted to Pro users. After I create it, I’ll give you full editing access. You’ll own the file and can independently reuse or modify it for future proposals, including changing the client information, content, and project details.

historical_evidence_messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’ve attached the proposal’s first draft. The Canva link is here: [URL_006]

Here are several notes for your review:

\- **General design:** Because the document became nearly twice its initial length and the timeline was short, I prioritized a cohesive design system instead of creating many distinct layouts. This should make the revisions more manageable as well.

\- **Graphics & photos:** I placed the images in organic-shaped frames and included a handful of understated graphic elements that seemed appropriate for the overall theme without distracting from the content.

\- **Section 6: Prioritization:** I didn’t find this section in the revised tables document, so I wasn’t certain whether it was still supposed to appear in the proposal.

\- **In-text bolding:** I wasn’t fully clear on which text was meant to be bold. Some content in the Google Doc was highlighted, while other text appeared in red, and during layout I couldn’t determine which formatting was deliberate and which was editorial markup.

\- **Links:** I checked every hyperlink, and they all seem to function. However, it would be helpful to have a second reviewer test each one too.

\- **Final review:** Given the very quick turnaround, I plan to make another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to identify anything I might have overlooked. I still wanted to deliver this to you today.

I’m looking forward to your feedback. Hopefully, the draft is in a strong place, and after your review I can fine-tune whatever you’d like changed.
